Conversion (did_convert) pruning funnel — win/loss classification

Real pipeline, single authoritative run Every stage below runs the actual conversion pipeline code (drop_correlated, the importance-screening XGBClassifier, prune_vif with its rank-deficiency and standardization fixes, exclude_leaky, train_model_clf's Optuna search maximizing CV ROC-AUC) — imported and executed unchanged, not reimplemented. Same row-selection as the ADR (quoted_adr) pipeline: 3 rows identified as genuine data-quality problems (B-202309-62288, B-202310-34967, B-202511-72086) are excluded, then a room_block>0 filter is applied, BEFORE the candidate pool is built — so both pipelines train on the same population and differ only in target/model type.

Candidate pool reaches the full 294. The raw transient-demand time series (Nexus_Transient_Demand_v2.csv) is joined for real via the pipeline's own join_transient() — a genuine per-row date-window average over the daily data, not an approximation. Nothing in the candidate pool is fabricated or backfilled. Every stage below (correlation pruning, importance screening, VIF pruning, leaky exclusion) runs the real, unmodified pipeline code on this complete pool, and the final 20-feature model is a genuine, freshly-trained fit.
Correlation with the target and multicollinearity among features are different things. In this run, nothing needed to be cut for that reason: every one of the 20 features that survived importance screening already had VIF < 10 on its own, so no strongly target-correlated feature got removed for being reconstructable from the others. (When that does happen in another run, this box names the specific feature and its real correlation instead of this note.)

Rows: 1,899 total → 3 flagged rows excluded → 1,896 → 1,702 after room_block>0 filter (194 meeting-only RFPs excluded).
Candidate pool 294 → correlation pruning (|r|≥0.85) → 188 → quick-XGBoost importance top-20 → VIF pruning (VIF≥10) → 20 → leaky-feature exclusion → 20 features trained.
All correlations on this page are real point-biserial (Pearson) r vs did_convert, n=1,702, computed directly from the training data. The 3 excluded rows are shown on every scatter as a hollow diamond marker, scored out-of-sample by the trained model.
